headline: BRENT HITS $100; GRAINS AND CATTLE FOLLOW
subheadline: US strikes on Iranian tankers push crude to a two-month high, dragging harvest input costs higher and lifting grains on war-premium buying.
lead: WTI settled at **$95.26**, its highest close in two months, after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck US forces in Jordan, the sharpest re-escalation of the Iran-Hormuz cycle since its July flare. Wheat added 11 cents on war-premium buying; harvest diesel has no global slack. The September WASDE lands Friday into a market that just re-priced risk. The next 48 hours are not quiet.
the_takeaway: Price your fall diesel needs now; the Hormuz premium is back and building.
teaser: Iranian tankers hit, Brent at $100, harvest diesel tightening. This is the session that matters.

one_number.context: India's refineries have run at 105-108% capacity for six months as diesel demand tightens global supply. With Middle East crude flows disrupted, every barrel India processes at that rate is one fewer available to cool the harvest diesel market in the US.

yesterdays_call.summary: Called wheat up toward $7.30; wheat closed today at $7.27, up 11 cents, but still 3 cents short of the target line.
yesterdays_call.note: Direction was right, level wasn't reached; war-premium buying moved wheat but not far enough.

sections.title: ENERGY LEADS THE COMPLEX
sections.body:
- WTI settled at **$95.26**, up 1.1% on the session, but the real story broke overnight: Brent crossed $100 after the US destroyed five Iranian tankers and Iran struck US forces in Jordan, the sharpest escalation in the Iran-Hormuz cycle since early July.
- Hedge funds have been piling into fuel contracts for weeks as Iran's export volumes have broke down and Hormuz traffic remains disrupted; today's news gave them every reason to hold.
- Harvest diesel is the input-cost pressure point right now: India running refineries at 108% capacity means global distillate supply has no slack, and that lands at the rack price for US producers filling tanks this month.
sections.catalyst: US destroys five Iranian tankers; Iran strikes US forces in Jordan; Brent breaks $100.
sections.bottom_line: Hormuz premium is back. Every day of harvest diesel unpriced is a risk decision, not a wait.
sections.farmer_action: If fall diesel needs are unpriced, today's Brent close above $100 says this is the window, not a reason to wait for a pullback.
sections.vs_yesterday: Crude: yesterday's $100 ceiling broke overnight on tanker strikes.

sections.title: WHEAT LIFTS ON WAR BID
sections.body:
- Chicago wheat added **11 cents** to $7.27, its best session in three weeks, with the catalyst clear: war-premium buying tied directly to the overnight Iran escalation and disrupted Black Sea-adjacent shipping sentiment.
- The move reclaims ground lost in last week's two consecutive 25-cent breaks, but the funds were net sellers for most of that slide; today's bid needs to hold through Friday's WASDE to confirm it's more than a reflex.
- Double-crop wheat-soybean profitability projections out of farmdoc today show 2027 planting intentions leaning toward wheat in southern Illinois, a slow-burn acreage tailwind that doesn't move this week's price but does change next year's supply math.
sections.catalyst: Iran escalation lifts energy and war-premium commodity bids; feedstuffs.com afternoon recap confirms wheat firm on geopolitical buying.
sections.bottom_line: One good session after two bad weeks is a bounce, not a trend. Friday's WASDE decides.
sections.vs_yesterday: Wheat: yesterday's breakdown reversed; war bid added 11 cents.

sections.title: CATTLE AND HOGS RUN HIGHER
sections.body:
- Live cattle at **$216.85** and feeders at $328.95 both firmed, with cattle up 1.8% and feeders up 1.3% on mild overnight strength that carried through the session.
- Lean hogs had their best day of the week, up 2.4% to $84.28; Smithfield's updated Q3 outlook, released this morning, showed Fresh Pork operating losses of $70-90M expected but Packaged Meats performing well, a mixed read that didn't slow the board.
- The Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still removes roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity; the processing-constrained dynamic keeps packer margins as the binding variable, not cattle numbers.
sections.catalyst: Smithfield Q3 Fresh Pork outlook miss; overnight cattle and hog strength carried by broader commodity bid.
sections.bottom_line: Cattle holding historic levels, hogs catching a bid. The Cargill lockout keeps supply tight at the plant.

sections.title: CORN FIRMS; BEANS HOLD NEAR HIGHS
sections.body:
- December corn added 4.5 cents to **$5.34**, firming alongside wheat on the commodity bid; early harvest pressure expected from Belt corn cutting hasn't materialized as a meaningful headwind yet.
- November soybeans added 9 cents to $13.19, sitting at 98% of their 52-week range with China's $17 billion annual US ag purchase commitment (May 18 deal, through 2028) still providing periodic floor support on confirmed sales.
- Soybean meal eased 1.2% and soyoil fell 2.1% as the meal/oil split continues to diverge; the soyoil weakness is worth watching into the WASDE Friday given biofuel policy sensitivity.
sections.catalyst: Broad commodity war-premium bid; China purchase commitment supports bean floor; soyoil weakness tied to biofuel margin pressure.
sections.bottom_line: Corn and beans riding the energy bid. WASDE Friday is the real test of whether these levels hold.

outside_the_pit.title: Tyson Plant Sale Dispute: Rollins vs. Tyson on American-Buyer Rule
outside_the_pit.body: USDA Secretary Rollins says Tyson committed to selling closed beef plants only to US buyers; Tyson publicly disputed that. Producers tracking packer concentration and processing capacity need to watch whether those plants reopen under domestic ownership or go dark permanently.

outside_the_pit.title: China Bird Flu Regionalization Costs US Chicken Producers $800M Annually
outside_the_pit.body: House members are pressing USTR to enforce China's Regionalization Agreement, which China applies inconsistently, blocking US poultry after any state-level outbreak. Until enforcement improves, that's $800M per year in export revenue left on the table for US chicken producers.

weekly_thread.question: Does the September WASDE confirm USDA's August yield cuts or does the big-acreage story overwhelm the yield miss?
weekly_thread.status_text: Geopolitical energy shock arrived first; grains caught a war bid that complicates clean reading of pre-WASDE positioning. Friday's report now lands into a hot market.

the_more_you_know.title: The meal/oil split is the soybean market's hidden fault line
the_more_you_know.body: Soybeans crushed at $13.01 produce both meal and oil, but today meal fell 1.2% while oil dropped 2.1%. When oil underperforms meal this sharply, crush margins compress on the oil side. That dynamic, tied to biofuel policy uncertainty ahead of the Farm Bill's September deadline, is quietly pressuring the soybean complex from inside even as the board holds near 52-week highs.

watch_list.desc: USDA September WASDE: corn yield above 181 bu/acre keeps carryout bearish pressure on; below 180 and the yield-cut story gets a second leg.
Brent crude: holding above $100 signals Hormuz premium is structural for harvest season; a pullback below $97 suggests the bid was a one-session reflex.
USDA Crop Progress: corn harvest pace above 10% would confirm Belt cutting is underway and could add early-harvest pressure to December futures.
Screwworm-driven closure of Mexican feeder cattle imports: Douglas, AZ phased reopening watch; feeder/live spread is the tell as returning supply hits the board.

daily_quote.text: Don't try to buy at the bottom and sell at the top. It can't be done except by liars.
